summary: Jane Robertson's October 3, 2023 article describes how businesses in the town of Elmwood responded to competition from the chain store MegaMart. They formed the Elmwood Business Alliance, adopted online tools, offered personalized experiences, ran education and outreach, and gained financial support from Mtiva Savings & Loan. The piece presents Elmwood as a model for other communities facing chain retailers.
one_line: Elmwood's local businesses band together through the Elmwood Business Alliance to survive MegaMart's arrival, offering a model for other towns.
key_facts: MegaMart, a chain giant, entered Elmwood's retail landscape as of September 15, causing a dip in foot traffic for local stores.
Mary Johnson owns the bookstore 'Leaf & Lore', which hosts storytelling sessions and book recommendations; she said "We're not just selling books, we're kindling a community."
The Elmwood Business Alliance (EBA) was formed on September 25 by local business owners, including Mary Johnson.
Tomás Herrera, a third-generation baker known for his sourdough, is a pivotal EBA member who caters events at Leaf & Lore.
Through autumn the EBA organized farmers' markets, bookstore readings, and shop local campaigns.
Jackie Simms of 'Handmade in Elmwood' used Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok to bring her crafts business to a global audience.
Digital storefronts, click-and-collect services, local delivery, and digital literacy workshops at EBA meetings helped shops compete on convenience.
Sarah Nguyen, a botanist, runs 'Green Thumbs Gardening', offering personalized garden planning consultations and monthly workshops.
The EBA launched an educational outreach program in local schools on November 5; volunteer Kenneth Davies, a retired history teacher, called Main Street 'living history'.
Mtiva Savings & Loan, led by President Angela Richardson, introduced tailored support programs for small business owners.
Max Feldman, owner of 'Melody Music Shop', is the EBA's event coordinator; seasonal fairs and art walks turned Main Street into a destination.
The EBA has begun investing in sustainability, with plans for green energy and waste reduction across Elmwood's businesses.
